record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: For perturbations of the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation of the form i u_t + u_xx + 2|u|²u + ε|u|^ℓ u = 0 with decaying initial data, especially when the unperturbed initial data produces a two-soliton solution, what is the long-time behavior of the perturbed solution?

evidence.quote: An open problem of great and basic interest is to analyze solutions of the Cauchy problem for perturbations of the focusing NLS equation ... Of particular interest is the case where f˜(x) corresponds to a 2-soliton solution for (unperturbed) focusing NLS.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the perturbed focusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on the real line:
$$ i\,u_t + u_{xx} + 2|u|^2 u + \varepsilon\,|u|^{\ell} u = 0, \qquad x\in\mathbb{R},\ t>0, $$
where $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter and $\ell>0$ with $\ell\neq 2$ (so the extra term is a genuine non-integrable perturbation of cubic focusing NLS). The initial data $u(x,0)=f(x)$ is assumed to be smooth and decaying at infinity (e.g. in Schwartz class).

Describe rigorously the long-time asymptotic behavior as $t\to\infty$ of the solution $u(x,t)$ to the Cauchy problem above, for general decaying initial data $f$, and in particular in the distinguished case where $f$ is the initial datum of a two-soliton solution of the unperturbed focusing cubic NLS equation
$$ i\,u_t + u_{xx} + 2|u|^2 u = 0. $$
The goal is to determine, in each space-time cone $x/t = \xi$ fixed, the leading-order asymptotics of $u(x,t)$ (including the modulation of soliton parameters such as amplitudes, velocities, positions, and phases, together with the radiation component) induced by the perturbation $\varepsilon|u|^\ell u$.
artifact.status_search_result: Long-time asymptotics for the unperturbed focusing cubic NLS have been substantially advanced (e.g., Borghese–Jenkins–McLaughlin and follow-ups using ∂̄-steepest descent yield soliton resolution in each space-time cone). However, the corresponding rigorous long-time asymptotic analysis for genuinely non-integrable perturbations of the form ε|u|^ℓ u with decaying data — particularly when the unperturbed datum produces a two-soliton — does not appear to have been carried out. Formal/integrable perturbation theory exists, but a rigorous treatment remains open.

status_evidence.title: Long Time Asymptotic Behavior of the Focusing Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation
status_evidence.snippet: DBAR generalization of the nonlinear steepest descent method ... leading order term in each cone is a multi-soliton whose parameters are modulated by soliton-soliton and soliton-radiation interactions.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous long-time asymptotics are known for unperturbed focusing NLS.

status_evidence.title: Integrable perturbation theory for dark solitons of the defocusing NLS
status_evidence.snippet: integrable perturbation theory for solitons of the NLS equation
status_evidence.claim: Perturbation theory for NLS solitons is actively studied but not in the rigorous long-time asymptotic regime requested.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress on Multi-bubble Blow-ups and Multi-solitons to (Stochastic) Focusing NLS
status_evidence.snippet: multi-solitons to focusing NLS with perturbations
status_evidence.claim: Multi-soliton dynamics under perturbations are an active research area, with results still partial.
